findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on file-not-found or I/O error
findings.failure_mode: entire program aborts when the shard file is missing or unreadable instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a typed error variant

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value or missing field
findings.failure_mode: corrupt shard data causes a panic rather than returning a typed ParseError the caller can recover from
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, use map_err on parse, and return a typed ParseError::InvalidValue for bad numeric data

findings.problem: Lossy as cast: u32 value cast to u16 via as u16, silently truncating values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 like 70000 becomes 4464 with no error, silently corrupting data
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| LoadError::Overflow) instead of as u16

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked array index accesses
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics with index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed ParseError::Invalid
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) returning None on missing fields, then map_err into a typed error

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is hidden I/O inside what should be pure data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: parsing function leaks logging side effect into the core, making it impossible to use without console output and breaking pure-data/Actions architecture
findings.fix: remove println! entirely; logging belongs in the shell layer, not in data loading

findings.problem: load_shards fuses file I/O, parsing, logging, and domain construction in a single infallible function returning Vec<Record>
findings.failure_mode: no error taxonomy exists; callers cannot distinguish file-not-found from parse errors from allocation failures; shell and calculation boundaries are violated
findings.fix: declare a typed enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError), Allocation }, return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, and isolate fs::read_to_string in the shell

findings.problem: Uses line.split(',').map().collect() into Vec<String> instead of the mandatory split_once pattern
findings.failure_mode: allocates a Vec of all parts unnecessarily; split_once is required for one-separator grammars per the hardening checklist
findings.fix: use let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; and parse value_str.trim()

findings.problem: No bounded allocation: no try_reserve, no domain cap on max_items, no checked capacity arithmetic on the output Vec
findings.failure_mode: a very large shard file can exhaust memory without a graceful allocation error; Vec grows unchecked
findings.fix: add a max_items parameter, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? after validation, and enforce the cap before pushing

findings.problem: Record uses status as raw String (pub name: String) instead of a newtype or domain value object
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct Record with arbitrary strings bypassing domain validation; illegal states are representable
findings.fix: wrap name in a named newtype like RecordName(String) with a smart constructor that validates the domain rules

findings.problem: Missing benchmark, profiler, allocation, and command-truth evidence
findings.failure_mode: no performance baseline, no allocation audit, no benchmark commands to validate correctness or speed claims
findings.fix: add a benchmark with workload description, baseline command, and measured numbers; add allocation audit with profiler evidence

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler evidence for hot-path analysis
no allocation audit showing try_reserve or bounded allocation usage
no command-truth evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: Review is static analysis only; no commands were run. The source contains 10 BLOCKER violations including panic surfaces (unwrap), unchecked indexing, lossy casts, hidden I/O, fused shell/calculation, missing error taxonomy, mandatory pattern violations, unbounded allocation, raw-primitive domain state, and missing evidence. All must be repaired before delivery.
